prompt: An online retailer's website traffic rose 30% this year, but orders were flat. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Traffic is up 30% and orders are flat.
options.feedback: This restates the facts without proposing a cause.

options.text: Conversion has likely fallen because the new traffic is lower-intent.
options.feedback: Right. It commits to a likely cause that fits the facts, and it is testable: I'd compare conversion rates by traffic source.

options.text: The new social media ads are bringing in the wrong visitors, and that is the whole story.
options.feedback: This states a cause as certain before any data has tested it.

options.text: The website isn't performing the way it should.
options.feedback: This is too vague to test: it doesn't say what is wrong or what data would show it.

explanation: More visits with the same orders means conversion fell. A good hypothesis picks the likeliest cause and the cut of data that tests it.

distractor_flaws.M.restates_facts: Traffic is up 30% and orders are flat.
distractor_flaws.M.overconfident_hypothesis: The new social media ads are bringing in the wrong visitors, and that is the whole story.
distractor_flaws.M.untestable_hypothesis: The website isn't performing the way it should.
